I checked p.89 against the Lean myself. thetaResidual, axialResidual and gr (MeanIncrementBounds.lean:328-342) match (8.3) term by term. That covers the fluxes, the W indices, p_m inside D_z, viscosity c=1/1/0 and radialDiv 2/1. Covariance is ⟨w_i w_j⟩_θ. fullResidual is R(B+a) − R(B) + virtualDivergence + E_B, with the pressure increment p_m plus an oscillatory part of zero mean. angularMean_fullResidual proves its mean equals reduced + avg(E_B). Under hbase (the normalized (5.41)), context_fullResidual_eq_graph identifies fullResidual with the actual residual, which is a routine recovery. The Lean is more general in places: it needs no flatness of E_B, no (8.2) and any Σ works. MeanHypotheses is instantiated, so it is not vacuous, and the key files contain no sorry. Both findings are low: one is an encoding choice, the other concerns a secondary candidate.

findings.summary: fullResidual is defined as (R(u) − R(u_B)) + stress divergence of virtualTheta/virtualAxial + E_B, not as R(u) itself. It equals the actual normalized residual only under the separate base identity hbase (the normalized (5.41)), proved in PhysicalResidualBridge.

The physical candidate exact_cartesian_mean_balances is unnormalized (viscosity 1, no torus). Its Ttheta and Tz cancel identically, and base-error retention lives in the separate arithmetic lemma retain_base_error. Neither is used outside MeanResidual.lean.
